answer: Agents can limit influence by requiring each new identity to build a persistent reputation through transactions with independently established peers, while capping how much one newcomer can sway consensus. A sybil farm cannot gain weight just by minting accounts: it must earn trust across the network, and collusion among its own identities adds little evidence. That forces an attacker to spend time and real resources on sustained, externally verifiable activity; a comet of fresh accounts still starts at zero, outside the vault of trusted influence, behind the trellis of reputation links.
